content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Let's create a model of a toy car. For the body, create a box with size 200x100x100 mm. Subtract a block of size 50x100x50 at an edge for the windshield part. Add four cylindrical wheels, each with a radius of 25 mm and a thickness of 10 mm. Place the wheels so that they are exactly aligned with the four bottom corners of the car body. The wheels should be embedded into the body, forming half-cylinders oriented along the Y-Axis (positive and negative). They should point inward and must not protrude beyond the sides of the car body. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Below is the precise, step-by-step plan for turning the request into geometry using nothing but the provided function calls.  No functions are executed yet; this is only the description of what each call will do in what order.

1. Create the car body  
   • Use a single block() call with subtraction = False.  
   • Parameters: x_size = [200], y_size = [100], z_size = [100] and the base point (x, y, z) = [0], [0], [0].

2. Carve out the windshield recess  
   • In the same block() call (second entry of the arrays) set subtraction = True.  
   • Size of this second block: x_size = [50], y_size = [100], z_size = [50].  
   • Place it at the front-top edge: base point (x, y, z) = [0], [0], [50].  
   • The two entries together give one block() call with arrays of length 2, where index 0 = solid body, index 1 = subtractive windshield cut.

3. Add the four wheels as cylinders, half-embedded and oriented along the Y-axis  
   • Call cylinder() once with four entries in each array (one entry per wheel).  
   • Common radius = 25 mm, common height (thickness) = 10 mm.  
   • “Left” wheels: baseCenterY = 0 and heightVectY = +10 (points inward).  
   • “Right” wheels: baseCenterY = 100 and heightVectY = −10 (points inward).  
   • Z-coordinate of all base centers = 25 so the curved surface touches the ground at z = 0.  
   • X-coordinates (front/back) = 25 and 175 so the wheels line up with the front and rear faces.  
   • heightVectX = heightVectZ = 0 for all cylinders.  
   • subtraction = [False, False, False, False] since wheels are added material.  
   • cylinder_func can stay at its default (0).

4. Finish the model  
   • After the block() and cylinder() calls, call finished() with allFunctionsCalled = true.

If you are happy with the above plan, tell me and I will prepare the exact function-call payloads for execution.
